what: Baseline: stage0 (profiling build of 32f22049) builds examples/http_server.ag cold in 9.8s at -O0 and 186s at -O2 (peak RSS 5.2 GB)
why: Establish the before value with the compiler's own --profile phases
evidence: `agc build examples/http_server.ag -O2 --no-cache --profile`: LLVM opt 44.5s, machine emit 137.5s, safety 2.7s

what: The -O0 profile is 63% LLVM SelectionDAG (AddNodeIDNode, popFromQueueImpl<src_ls_rr_sort>) plus 17% MovePath::get_or_create_child/memcmp
why: Superlinear LLVM passes point at huge basic blocks; the move-path hotspot points at huge place trees

what: --emit-llvm is 167 MB; h2_serve_conn, HttpClient.request and h2_get each hold one basic block of about 361K instructions
why: Find what generates the giant blocks
evidence: IR shows `alloca [36121 x {ptr, ptr, i32, i8}]`: one runtime owner node per element of H2Stream.hbuf (u8[4096]) x 8 streams, each initialized with unrolled GEPs and stores

what: An array whose element type owns nothing (not move-tracked) is one owner node; its elements get no owner nodes
why: Copy elements can never be moved out, so per-element state only bloats every declaration (O(N) stores) and transition (O(siblings) loads). Rust also treats arrays as a single unit for init/move analysis
evidence: OwnerLayouts::tracks_elements is the single predicate for the layout builder and codegen

what: Elements of an untracked array carry no owner state (place state None); only whole-array writes and moves change the array's state
why: Alternative was to let an element write mark the whole array initialized. That changes behavior for the common field-by-field construction of HttpStream/HttpConnection; "None" matches the old behavior for every stdlib pattern (tls_state never written, key_host partially written). Declarations without an initializer are zero-filled, so no undefined bytes are exposed either way
evidence: grep of the four Drop-owning stdlib types with no-drop arrays and their uninitialized declarations

what: The first collapse alone crashed 10 HTTP tests (SIGSEGV): lvalue resolution projected owner state into the collapsed array's (null) child list at runtime
why: project_reference_state follows the node's first-child pointer for every index
result: fixed by gating the projection on tracks_elements

what: Bump the stage0 cache identity to borrow-state-abi2
why: Tracked references walk owner-node child offsets across function boundaries, so cached objects built with the old layout are ABI-incompatible

what: The test runner and default builds share ~/.cache/silver keyed only by version+SHA+ABI string, so a modified compiler at the same commit reuses another compiler's objects
why: A baseline run that reused new-compiler objects reported 10 failures that were not its own
evidence: Re-running both compilers with isolated XDG_CACHE_HOME: baseline 117/117 pass

what: Owner-array collapse: -O0 9.8s -> 1.9s, -O2 186s -> 3.0s, peak RSS 5.2 GB -> 388 MB; stdlib suite 117 pass / 1 skip (same as baseline); http_server -O0/-O2 binaries serve /plaintext, /json and /echo
why: Prove behavior at the real boundary, not only the build
evidence: tests/run_tests.py with isolated caches; curl against the built server

what: Legacy field drop flags and array drop glue return early for types without drop glue, and array drop glue is a runtime loop
why: register_field_drops emitted one dead GEP per element (141K for u8[65536]); emit_drop_glue_at_pointer unrolled per element

what: Remaining codegen cost is real IR volume: 61% of named instructions are owner/reference state machinery (descriptor init ~19K, ancestor recompute ~30K, reference projection ~9K)
why: Ancestor summaries reload every sibling per transition: a 23-field constructor emits 23x23 load/compare chains. The owner alloca escapes (it stores pointers into itself), so -O2 cannot fold it
evidence: opt with the compiler's -O2 pipeline still leaves 317 state loads in HttpRequest.new

what: Owner runtime v2: owner nodes are {i32 parent, i32 first_child, i32 child_count, i8 state} with node-relative offsets, initialized by one memcpy from a deduplicated private template; set/transition/project are shared internal helpers instead of inline load/compare chains
why: Ancestor recompute and descriptor init were per-site unrolled code (D11). Relative offsets make the template position-independent so a single constant can initialize every declaration of the same layout

what: The -O2 build crashed in AlwaysInliner fixupLineNumbers: every helper instruction carried `!dbg !{}`
why: inkwell's get_current_debug_location wraps an unset location as an empty MDNode, and restoring it stamped that node on later instructions
result: fixed with ParkedBuilder (raw LLVMGetCurrentDebugLocation2/LLVMSetCurrentDebugLocation2), also used by task drop glue

what: finalize_debug() runs before the LLVM opt pipeline
why: The inliner rewrites debug locations, so debug metadata must be final before opt runs

what: lower_aggregate_copies: stores of >=32-byte struct/array SSA values become memset (zero), memcpy from a private constant (other constants), memmove (single-use load in the same block with no write in between), or are erased (undef/poison)
why: LLVM scalarizes first-class aggregate stores element by element (instcombine at -O2, SelectionDAG at -O0) and they defeat FastISel; a 40 KB zero-initialized local became ~1000 stores in one block
evidence: http_server --no-cache: -O0 1.86 s -> 1.28 s, -O2 3.02 s -> 1.57 s (single runs, profiling build)

what: The intrinsics claim alignment 1
why: Codegen stores enum payloads at offset 2 of `{ i16, [N x i8] }` with the payload type's alignment (16 for i128); the memset/memmove inherited it and emitted movaps on a misaligned address (serialize_containers_test SIGSEGV). Unaligned moves cost the same on aligned x86-64 data
evidence: gdb: movaps to rax-0x1e in WideNums__from_json; IR `store %WideNums ..., ptr %enum.data214, align 16`
result: fixed; latent under-alignment of enum payloads (UB before this branch too) recorded as F01

what: Enum payloads are laid out at offset 2 (`{ i16, [N x i8] }`) but loaded/stored with the payload type's ABI alignment
why: Undefined behavior that LLVM happened to lower with scalar moves. Fixing it changes the enum layout ABI in stage0 and stage1, outside this task

what: glibc malloc/free/consolidate took ~30% of an -O0 build; LD_PRELOAD mimalloc 1.36 s -> 1.04 s (median of 5), jemalloc 1.10 s
why: The frontend clones and drops AST nodes at a high rate; allocator cost is a symptom, the clones are the cause (D19, D20, D22)

what: mimalloc is the Rust global allocator of the agc binary
why: Same choice rustc makes with jemalloc. mimalloc measured faster than jemalloc here; LLVM keeps glibc malloc. Cost: about +60 MB peak RSS on http_server (270 -> 340 MB)

what: Function doc comments are collected only for textual IR output
why: Program::doc_comment_for scans every comment and every item per item (cubic) and ran for every object build although only --emit-llvm prints the comments

what: Generic impl templates are shared through Rc, and a template method body is cloned only when its instance is missing
why: try_instantiate_generic_impl_method_for_type_filtered deep-copied every generic impl template (all method bodies) on every call; get_drop_function_name calls it from every owner, drop-flag and cleanup site. 70% of ExpressionKind clones came from this path
evidence: gdb sampling of ExpressionKind::clone call sites (1.98M clones); IR generation 288 ms -> 94 ms, -O0 total 1.10 s -> 0.82 s

what: Backtrace line/argument tables are written into the emitted ELF object instead of re-emitting the module. Pass 1 reserves the four table symbols in section .data.silver_bt; afterwards bt_tables::write_into_elf rewrites only that section and its RELA section (function addresses relocate against the object's own function symbols, internal ones included; pointers relocate against the section symbol; the relocation kind is copied from LLVM's own entries). Any unmet precondition (COFF, Mach-O, wasm, assembly output) falls back to the old re-emit
why: The second emit doubled machine-code generation for every debug build. Alternatives rejected: a second object (changes the single-object contract of every caller and the cache), `ld -r` (needs a host linker for the target during compilation), appending sections/symbols (renumbers symbol indices referenced by 23 GROUP and 32 RELA sections)
evidence: -O0 machine emit 2x158 ms -> 160 ms + 0.3 ms write; backtrace output (lines, files, args of a private function) identical to baseline

what: Unit objects (emit_bt_tables=false) skip DWARF parsing and the table step entirely
why: They carry no tables, yet the debug path re-emitted an identical module for every cached unit

what: Constant array initializers use the element type for inkwell's new_const_array
why: All three call sites passed the array type, building `[N x [N x T]]` constants with T operands. The in-memory module was invalid (bitcode reader: "Incorrect type in array initializer"); codegen emitted the right bytes by accident
evidence: in-process initializer type check on hpack_static_names/values

what: Monomorph rewrites every generic function call site in one program walk
why: instantiate_requests walked the whole program once per function request. Rules are keyed by template name and the first matching rule in request order wins, as before. Method rewrites only read receivers/let annotations and only write method-call nodes, so moving the function walk after them is equivalent

what: Link time depends on the shell: inside `nix develop` ld.lld is on PATH (~13 ms); outside, the driver falls back to the Nix cc wrapper (25 realpath spawns + ld.bfd, ~57 ms)
why: Benchmarks must run in one environment
result: all benchmarks run inside nix develop

what: Monomorph requests share the typeck template through Arc (function source, impl block, method) instead of deep-copying it per call site; the two passes that edit request templates (default normalization, body refresh) update each distinct shared template once and reuse the result
why: Every generic method call site copied its whole impl block with all method bodies. Exactness: refresh keys an impl copy by (template, method name), so each method still gets its own impl copy as before, and the last matching impl block still wins
evidence: typeck 67 ms -> 47 ms, monomorph 67 ms -> 46 ms, peak RSS 343 MB -> 286 MB; suite 117/1

what: Parallel codegen upper bound: llvm-split + concurrent llc on the exact pre-emit module (llc times include re-parsing text IR). -O0: 224 ms (1 part) -> 82 ms (4); -O2: 518 ms -> 197 ms (8, limited by the largest function)
why: Decide whether splitting the module across threads is worth per-thread contexts, bitcode round trips, internal-symbol promotion and object merging
result: deferred: estimated in-process gain 65 ms at -O0 and 225 ms at -O2
